question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative inverse of $5$ modulo $9,$ denoted ${5}^{-1},$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
5\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,9).
$$

Note that since $\text{gcd}(5,9)=1,$ an inverse element exists and is unique up to congruence modulo $9.$

Since the modulus $n=9$ is small, we can find the inverse $x$ by computing exponents of $5$ (modulo $9$) until we get a result of $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2} & ≡5\cdot 5≡25≡2\cdot 9+7≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ {5}^{3} & ≡5\cdot 7≡35≡3\cdot 9+8≡8 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ {5}^{4} & ≡5\cdot 8≡40≡4\cdot 9+4≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ {5}^{5} & ≡5\cdot 4≡20≡2\cdot 9+2≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,9) \\ {5}^{6} & ≡5\cdot 2≡10≡9+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,9)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $5\cdot 2≡1\,(\text{mod}\,9).$ Therefore, the multiplicative inverse of $5$ modulo $9$ is $2.$
